name: Camping 101: Leatherworking

angles.text: A campfire is the heart of a wilderness campsite. Basic cooking teaches you to kindle a flame and sustain a camp in the wild.

faq.answer: Townsfolk frown on tents pitched in streets or city squares, so take your tent beyond the city gates and into the wilderness.
faq.q: Where can you pitch a camp tent?

faq.answer: A tent alone is not a full camp. You also need a campfire burning beside it.
faq.q: What else is required besides a tent to pitch a camp?

faq.answer: Culinary masters and cooking trainers teach you to kindle a campfire as part of preparing food. Seek a cooking trainer to learn the basics.
faq.q: Where do adventurers learn to build a campfire?

faq.answer: Leatherworkers use cured hides and pelts, joined with sturdy stitching, to make tent coverings that can withstand rough wilderness elements. This craft gives wanderers a reliable shelter from animal hides.
faq.q: How does leatherworking relate to crafting camp tents?

faq.answer: Wilderness camps give travelers a secure haven to rest and recuperate when they are far from settled outposts, inns and settlements. Portable shelter and a warm fire help against the elements and perilous terrain.
faq.q: Why do adventurers establish camps in the wilderness?

aliases: why cant i pitch tent in city
faq.answer: Townsfolk object because tents across public streets clutter thoroughfares and cause disturbances. Settlements have inns and private lodgings for travelers, so locals expect camps to remain in the wild.
faq.q: Why do townsfolk object to setting up tents inside town?

sections.body: For tradespeople who work with hides and leather, making a shelter of their own is an essential milestone. A sturdy leather tent shields travelers from harsh weather, wind and the chill of night on open ground. Townsfolk frown on tents pitched in crowded streets or market squares, so you need to pass beyond the city gates and into the wilderness to make camp.
sections.title: Pitching Shelter in the Wild

sections.body: A pitched tent is only half a campsite. A proper fire keeps back darkness and cold winds, and gives you a hearth in dangerous lands. Since cooking in the field begins with building and tending a fire, seek instruction from culinary masters and cooking trainers. They teach you to kindle a campfire before you establish camp.
sections.title: The Warmth of a Campfire

summary: At a camp in the wilderness, leatherworkers put cured hides to use and make shelter of their own. A sound campsite needs a pitched tent and a fire, whose kindling is taught by cooking trainers.
